title: Young Adult Cancer Survivors’ (YACS) Perspectives on Decision-Making During and After Cancer Treatment
summary:
A cancer diagnosis during young adulthood confronts patients with numerous difficult decisions. Treatment decisions, in particular, can have a long-term impact on their lives. Even years after completing cancer treatment, some survivors may regret their previous treatment decisions.
This study aims to investigate the extent to which young adult cancer survivors regret their previous treatment decisions and to identify factors associated with such regret. These include quality of life, psychological well-being, involvement in treatment decisions, social support, and potential long-term effects of cancer treatment.
Individuals who were aged 18 to 39 years at the time of their cancer diagnosis and whose initial diagnosis was at least five years ago will be invited to complete a one-time anonymous online questionnaire. Completion of the questionnaire takes approximately 20 to 30 minutes.
The findings are intended to help improve counselling, treatment, and long-term care for young people diagnosed with cancer.

interventions.name: One-time anonymous online survey of long-term young adult cancer survivors using standardised and study-specific questionnaires administered via LimeSurvey. Completion takes approximately 20–30 minutes. No therapeutic intervention is provided.
